<a id="welcome-to-slackblocks"></a>
# Welcome to `slackblocks`!

<p align="center">
  <img width="30%" src="/slackblocks/img/legacy/081da8626e0988b4a2683f4ed6644eb01e32569c/sb.png" />
</p>

`slackblocks` is a Python library for building Slack messages with the [Block Kit API](https://api.slack.com/block-kit) — without writing JSON by hand.

It exists because Block Kit JSON is verbose, easy to get subtly wrong, and unpleasant to maintain in source control. `slackblocks` gives you:

- **Typed Python classes** for every block, element, and object Slack supports.
- **Validation as you build** — character limits, required fields, mutually-exclusive options, and element-type restrictions are enforced at construction time, so you find out *before* hitting Slack's API.
- **Drop-in compatibility** with both the official [`slack-sdk`](https://pypi.org/project/slack-sdk/) and the legacy [`slackclient`](https://pypi.org/project/slackclient/) — unpack a `Message` directly into `client.chat_postMessage(**message)`.
- **Zero runtime dependencies.**

## Quickstart {#quickstart}

```bash
pip install slackblocks
```

```python
from slackblocks import HeaderBlock, Message, SectionBlock, DividerBlock

message = Message(
    channel="#general",
    blocks=[
        HeaderBlock("Build #482 passed :white_check_mark:"),
        SectionBlock("All 1,247 tests green in 3m 12s."),
        DividerBlock(),
        SectionBlock("*Author:* @nick  •  *Branch:* `main`"),
    ],
)

print(message.json())
```

See the [installation guide](/v2.0.0/usage/installation) and [sending messages guide](/v2.0.0/usage/sending_messages) to take it from here.

## Components {#components}

The [Slack Block Kit API](https://api.slack.com/block-kit) defines several resource types (all defined in JSON) that work together to build block-based messages. `slackblocks` mirrors that hierarchy with Python classes.

### Objects {#objects}

[Objects](/v2.0.0/reference/objects) (e.g. [`Text`](/v2.0.0/reference/objects#objects.Text), [`Option`](/v2.0.0/reference/objects#objects.Option), [`Confirm`](/v2.0.0/reference/objects#objects.Confirm)) are the lowest-level primitives — small composable pieces that populate [Elements](/v2.0.0/reference/elements) and [Blocks](/v2.0.0/reference/blocks).

For convenience, [`PlainText`](/v2.0.0/reference/objects#objects.PlainText) and [`Markdown`](/v2.0.0/reference/objects#objects.Markdown) are thin subclasses of `Text` that you can use anywhere a `Text` is expected — `PlainText("Hi", emoji=True)` reads more naturally than `Text("Hi", type_=TextType.PLAINTEXT, emoji=True)`.

### Elements {#elements}

[Elements](/v2.0.0/reference/elements) are typically interactive UI controls that go *inside* blocks. The [`CheckboxGroup`](/v2.0.0/reference/elements#elements.CheckboxGroup) element, for instance, takes one or more [`Option`](/v2.0.0/reference/objects#objects.Option) items and presents a checkbox menu.

### Blocks {#blocks}

[Blocks](/v2.0.0/reference/blocks) are the core visual unit of a message. Different block classes produce different UI:

- [`SectionBlock`](/v2.0.0/reference/blocks#blocks.SectionBlock) — a chunk of markdown text, optionally with an accessory element.
- [`HeaderBlock`](/v2.0.0/reference/blocks#blocks.HeaderBlock) — a large bold title.
- [`DividerBlock`](/v2.0.0/reference/blocks#blocks.DividerBlock) — a visual separator (like an HTML `<hr>`).
- [`MarkdownBlock`](/v2.0.0/reference/blocks#blocks.MarkdownBlock) — GitHub-flavored Markdown (Slack 2024+; richer formatting than `mrkdwn`).
- [`RichTextBlock`](/v2.0.0/reference/blocks#blocks.RichTextBlock) — formatted text with inline styling, lists, code blocks, and quotes.
- [`ActionsBlock`](/v2.0.0/reference/blocks#blocks.ActionsBlock) — a row of interactive elements like buttons or menus.
- [`VideoBlock`](/v2.0.0/reference/blocks#blocks.VideoBlock) — embed a video from a Slack-supported provider.
- [`ImageBlock`](/v2.0.0/reference/blocks#blocks.ImageBlock), [`ContextBlock`](/v2.0.0/reference/blocks#blocks.ContextBlock), [`InputBlock`](/v2.0.0/reference/blocks#blocks.InputBlock), [`FileBlock`](/v2.0.0/reference/blocks#blocks.FileBlock), [`TableBlock`](/v2.0.0/reference/blocks#blocks.TableBlock).

See [Using Blocks](/v2.0.0/usage/using_blocks) for examples of all block types side-by-side with their JSON output and Slack rendering.

### Messages {#messages}

[Messages](/v2.0.0/reference/messages) are a convenience wrapper around blocks that can be unpacked directly into the Slack SDK's `chat_postMessage` (and friends).

- [`Message`](/v2.0.0/reference/messages#messages.Message) — a normal channel message.
- [`WebhookMessage`](/v2.0.0/reference/messages#messages.WebhookMessage) — for incoming webhooks.
- [`MessageResponse`](/v2.0.0/reference/messages#messages.MessageResponse) — replies to slash commands and interactions.

### Views {#views}

[Views](/v2.0.0/reference/views) are an alternative usage of blocks that build custom UI surfaces in Slack — modal dialogs and the App Home tab — typically used by interactive Slack apps.

### Utilities {#utilities}

- [`block_kit_builder_url(payload, team_id=None)`](/v2.0.0/reference/utils#builder.block_kit_builder_url) — turn any block, list of blocks, message, or view into a [Block Kit Builder](https://app.slack.com/block-kit-builder) URL for browser-based preview.
- [`Block.from_dict(data)`](/v2.0.0/reference/blocks#blocks.Block.from_dict) — parse a Slack-shaped block payload back into a `slackblocks` object. Per-class `from_dict` parsers are also available on every composition object.
